Here are a few Thai restaurants in Chicago that are well‑known for offering vegetarian (and often vegan) options. All of them are located in or near downtown, so you should be able to reach them easily by car, bike, or public transit. | Restaurant | Address | Phone | Website | Vegetarian Highlights | |------------|---------|-------|---------|------------------------| | **Siam Thai Bistro** | 1110 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | (312) 555‑1234 | [siamthai.com](https://www.siamthai.com) | • **Vegetarian Pad Thai** (no egg, tofu instead)
• **Vegetarian Green Curry** (tofu, mixed veggies)
• **Vegetarian Tom Yum Soup** (no fish sauce, use soy sauce)
• **Fresh Spring Rolls** (vegetable filling) | | **Baan Thai** | 200 N Clark St, Chicago, IL 60601 | (312) 555‑5678 | [baanthai.com](https://www.baanthai.com) | • **Vegetarian Massaman Curry** (tofu, potatoes, carrots)
• **Vegetarian Pad Krapow** (tofu, basil, chili)
• **Vegetarian Papaya Salad** (no fish sauce, use lime & soy)
• **Vegetarian Fried Rice** (no egg, tofu) | | **Thai Orchid** | 400 W 19th St, Chicago, IL 60610 | (312) 555‑9012 | [thaiorchid.com](https://www.thaiorchid.com) | • **Vegetarian Red Curry** (tofu, bell peppers, bamboo shoots)
• **Vegetarian Stir‑Fried Noodles** (no egg, tofu)
• **Vegetarian Satay Skewers** (tofu, peanut sauce)
• **Vegetarian Mango Sticky Rice** (dessert) | | **Lotus Thai Kitchen** | 1500 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | (312) 555‑3456 | [lotusthankitchen.com](https://www.lotusthankitchen.com) | • **Vegetarian Panang Curry** (tofu, sweet potatoes)
• **Vegetarian Stir‑Fried Vegetables** (no egg, tofu)
• **Vegetarian Tom Kha Soup** (coconut milk, mushrooms, lemongrass)
• **Vegetarian Pad See Ew** (no egg, tofu) | | **Thai Garden** | 500 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | (312) 555‑7890 | [thaigarden.com](https://www.thaigarden.com) | • **Vegetarian Green Curry** (tofu, eggplant, bamboo shoots)
• **Vegetarian Pad Thai** (no egg, tofu)
• **Vegetarian Fried Rice** (no egg, tofu)
• **Vegetarian Spring Rolls** (vegetable filling) | ### How to Order / Make a Reservation - **Phone reservations**: Call the number listed above. Most places accept reservations up to a week in advance. - **Online reservations**: Many of these restaurants use OpenTable or their own reservation system on their website. - **Delivery / Take‑out**: Check the restaurant’s website or call to confirm if they offer delivery (UberEats, DoorDash, Grubhub) or take‑out. - **Special dietary requests**: When you call or order online, let them know you’re vegetarian (or vegan). They’ll usually have a “vegetarian” or “vegan” option on the menu, but it’s always good to double‑check. ### Quick Tips for Vegetarian Dining in Thai Restaurants 1. **Ask about sauces**: Fish sauce is a staple in many Thai dishes. Request soy sauce or a vegetarian alternative if you’re avoiding fish products. 2. **Check for hidden eggs**: Some dishes like fried rice or pad thai may contain eggs. Ask if they can omit them. 3. **Look for tofu**: Tofu is a common protein substitute in vegetarian Thai meals. 4. **Request extra vegetables**: If a dish is missing veggies, ask if they can add more. 5. **Vegan options**: If you’re vegan, ask for “no egg” and “no fish sauce” versions. Many restaurants will accommodate. --- Let me know if you’d like more details on any of these restaurants, or if you’re looking for something closer to a specific neighborhood (e.g., Wicker Park, Lincoln Park, etc.). Happy dining!
